html:
The fragile Middle East ceasefire has dramatically collapsed, marked by intensifying US and Iranian strikes across the region, triggering fears of a return to all-out war. These renewed hostilities coincided with the high-profile burial of Ali Khamenei in Mashhad, an event framed by some as a symbol of resistance.

US-Iran Conflict: The United States launched new airstrikes against Iran, with Centcom reporting hits on 90 Iranian targets since Tuesday. In retaliation, Iran fired missiles at Bahrain, Qatar, Kuwait, and Jordan, targeting countries hosting US forces, resulting in one injury reported in Kuwait. Reports also indicated explosions near Iran's nuclear power plant and Iranian oil tankers rapidly leaving the Strait of Hormuz amid fears of potential blockades. Despite the escalation, a US official stated that "technical talks" with Iran are ongoing, with Washington committed to finding a resolution, a sentiment contradicted by Trump who stated the ceasefire was "over." Israel declared its readiness to attack Iran for a "third time if necessary."

Great Power Politics: President Trump wrapped up a NATO summit in Turkey on a positive note, meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and announcing the U.S. will provide Ukraine a license to make Patriot air defense systems. Separately, Donald Trump terminated the remaining members of the Election Assistance Commission, just months before midterm elections, inciting fears of "chaos." China demonstrated its growing military capabilities with a ballistic missile launch in the Pacific, which the US noted was given only hours' warning.

Economic Developments: Chip giant SK Hynix successfully raised $26.5 billion in a mega US share sale, with shares set to debut on the Nasdaq as the largest ever by a foreign firm. Meanwhile, oil prices have decreased amidst the escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran. In other news, Telstra’s chief executive apologized for a recent outage, admitting the company knew of the risks of time-keeping failure, as South Australian police investigate a death that occurred during the network issues.

European Affairs & Environment: A severe heatwave continues to grip southern Europe, with wildfires in Spain killing twelve people in the province of Almería and scorching temperatures also reported in Paris during Haute Couture Week. Pressure is building on Europe's biggest port, Rotterdam, to accelerate its transition to greener operations, facing a lawsuit demanding reduced dependence on fossil fuel firms. Andy Burnham, mayor of Manchester, is increasingly seen as the UK's likely next prime minister, signaling intentions to alter Britain's policy towards Israel, potentially including sanctions.

Other Global Incidents: A factory fire in China's "shoe capital" killed at least 28 people, while in Australia, a deadly H5 flu was found in a local bird for the first time. The UN human rights chief called for an immediate halt to fighting in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo following intensified clashes between the army and the Rwanda-backed M23 militia in South Kivu, where the Ebola death toll has risen to 625.
